title: A New Mexico Community Was a Place to Build a Life. Then a Hypersonic Missile Factory Showed Up
gist: Castelion, a $13B defense-tech startup founded by ex-SpaceX executives, is building 'Project Ranger', a 1,000-acre hypersonic missile factory in New Mexico just over 1,000 yards from ~450 low-income homes, backed by $125M in county bonds and a 95% property-tax discount. Public records show unresolved fire-safety terms during construction, a Sandia hazard report with failed redactions, and Navy contracts implying ~$3.3M per Blackbeard missile versus a $384,000 advertised price.

insights.claim: Castelion, founded in November 2022 by three former SpaceX executives, has reached a $13 billion valuation, more than four times its $2.8 billion Series B valuation from last year.
insights.speaker: Yulia Almazova
insights.so_what: Signals extreme private-market appetite for defense-tech, especially hypersonics; valuation step-ups are steep.
insights.quote: The company has recently hit a valuation of $13 billion—more than four times its Series B valuation of $2.8 billion from last year.
insights.locator: Big PlansCastelion has become a bit

insights.claim: Castelion has received over $500 million in US military contracts in just 18 months and is one of the 'Arsenal of Freedom' suppliers.
insights.speaker: Yulia Almazova
insights.so_what: Rapid contract accumulation validates the low-cost-munitions thesis for new-entrant defense primes.
insights.quote: It has received over $500 million in US military contracts in just 18 months

insights.claim: In September the Navy awarded Castelion its largest contract yet, worth up to $200 million.
insights.speaker: Yulia Almazova
insights.so_what: Continuing Navy commitment despite cost overruns indicates strong demand signal for hypersonics.
insights.quote: And most recently, in September, the Navy awarded Castelion the company’s largest contract yet—up to $200 million.

insights.claim: Castelion broke ground on the 1,000-acre Project Ranger facility on January 21, bills it as America's largest dedicated hypersonic manufacturing facility, expects construction complete by year-end, and targets mass production as early as next year.
insights.speaker: Yulia Almazova
insights.so_what: Mass production timeline in 2027 is a key milestone for Castelion's valuation and hypersonic supply.
insights.quote: The company broke ground on the 1,000-acre facility on January 21, and it’s targeting mass production as early as next year.
insights.locator: Project Ranger will become Castelion’s biggest

insights.claim: Castelion pitches cheap hypersonics: its Blackbeard missile was set to sell for $384,000 per unit, versus an estimated $41 million per missile for the Army's Dark Eagle per a 2023 CBO study.
insights.speaker: Yulia Almazova
insights.so_what: A ~100x cost gap is the core investment thesis behind attritable hypersonic weapons startups.
insights.quote: Castelion’s main product, Blackbeard, is a solid-rocket-powered missile that was set to sell for $384,000 per unit.
insights.locator: The firm touts its ability to make hypersonic

insights.claim: Navy contracts for the first 50 Blackbeard prototypes total $163.4 million (about $50M + $23.4M + $90M), or roughly $3.3 million per missile, far above the advertised $384,000 unit price.
insights.speaker: Yulia Almazova
insights.so_what: Real unit costs ~8.6x above the pitch undermine the low-cost hypersonic narrative; watch for production-scale cost evidence.
insights.quote: pushing the total to $163.4 million for 50 missiles, or $3.3 million per unit.

insights.claim: Castelion has released a photo of Blackbeard but no public test data or concrete performance figures to verify the weapon's efficacy.
insights.speaker: Yulia Almazova
insights.so_what: Valuation is running ahead of verifiable performance, a key diligence risk.
insights.quote: Castelion has not publicly released any test data to verify its weapon’s efficacy.
insights.locator: Recently, Castelion released the first photo

insights.claim: WIRED cites a June ammonium perchlorate rocket-motor explosion at Anduril's Mississippi facility as underscoring the technical risks of scaling solid-propellant production.
insights.speaker: Yulia Almazova
insights.so_what: Solid-rocket-motor scaling is a sector-wide execution and safety risk for defense-tech entrants.
insights.quote: underscored the technical risks of scaling solid propellant production.
insights.locator: Such events are hardly unheard of.

themes.theme: Safety hazards and governance gaps at Project Ranger

insights.claim: The Project Ranger site appears to sit a little over 1,000 yards from roughly 450 properties in Rio Rancho Estates, putting them within a danger zone if stored explosive chemicals catch fire.
insights.speaker: Yulia Almazova
insights.so_what: Proximity creates legal, permitting and reputational risk that could delay or constrain operations.
insights.locator: The company’s chosen site for its mega-campus

insights.claim: A Sandia National Labs hazard report says Castelion plans to store up to 250,000 pounds of ammonium perchlorate in magazines and up to 81,000 pounds of active explosive material in integration facilities; a worst-case detonation could shatter large windows almost four miles away.
insights.speaker: Yulia Almazova
insights.so_what: Quantifies tail-risk exposure that could trigger community opposition, insurance cost or regulatory action.
insights.locator: It identifies a massive “storage facility fire”

insights.claim: The Rio Rancho Fire Department determined that 17 of the 26 buildings at Project Ranger would be left to burn in a fire, and a chemical fire would release toxic hydrogen chloride and chlorine gas.
insights.speaker: Yulia Almazova
insights.so_what: Highlights unmitigated operational hazards at a key hypersonic production node.
insights.quote: the Rio Rancho Fire Department determined 17 of the 26 buildings at the Project Ranger site would be left to burn if a fire ignited
insights.locator: Emails obtained through public records requests

insights.claim: Emails show Castelion was still negotiating fire-flow requirements with Rio Rancho between March and May after construction began, and the city manager replaced the requirements with a promise that hard numbers would come later, which CFO Andrew Kreitz welcomed as saving legal bills.
insights.speaker: Yulia Almazova
insights.so_what: Lax permitting may speed buildout but raises later regulatory and litigation risk.
insights.quote: “Great news! Saves all of us both legal bills and headaches,” Kreitz wrote in response.
insights.locator: After a few weeks, the requirements were replaced

insights.claim: Sandia's FOIA release of the hazard report was 'redacted' by putting black highlight over black text, leaving the full report retrievable by copy-paste.
insights.speaker: Yulia Almazova
insights.so_what: Shows weak information controls around defense-industrial projects.
insights.quote: the lab simply put black ink highlight over black text, leaving the full unredacted report accessible via copying and pasting.
insights.locator: Under the Freedom of Information Act

insights.claim: One of the Sandia hazard report's authors, Meg Davidson, has since left Sandia and now works as senior manager of strategic partnerships at Castelion.
insights.speaker: Yulia Almazova
insights.so_what: Revolving-door ties between national labs and defense startups may draw scrutiny.
insights.locator: Sandia declined to provide comment for WIRED.

insights.claim: Castelion first applied in August 2023 to build a rocket factory in Churchill County, Nevada, under the name Pallas Industrials, then withdrew after officials demanded testing conditions and safety protocols, and moved to New Mexico.
insights.speaker: Yulia Almazova
insights.so_what: Suggests defense startups shop for jurisdictions with lighter safety scrutiny.

themes.theme: Subsidies and state-backed defense industrial policy

insights.claim: Sandoval County approved $125 million in industrial revenue bonds, granted Castelion a 95 percent property-tax discount and abated compensating taxes on out-of-state equipment to land Project Ranger.
insights.speaker: Yulia Almazova
insights.so_what: Generous local subsidies lower capex for defense-tech manufacturing and illustrate competition among states for these plants.
insights.quote: The commissioners granted an astounding 95 percent discount on what Castelion would normally owe in property taxes.

insights.claim: New Mexico's top political figures, including Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham and US senator Martin Heinrich, attended the groundbreaking while residents were not invited, and residents say the deal was done before it became public.
insights.speaker: Yulia Almazova
insights.so_what: Bipartisan political backing reduces near-term project risk but fuels local backlash.
insights.quote: “All of this happened behind the scenes. By the time it was public, it was already a done deal,”
insights.locator: Castelion held its first public information meeting
